ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Photosynthetic activity can vary with both light intensities and leaf temperature. Solid lines in the following graph plot the rate of photosynthesis as a function of carbon dioxide uptake, leaf temperature, and light intensity. The dashed line plots the rate of respiration that occurs at the same time as photosynthesis. The compensation point occurs when photosynthesis and respiration rates are equal. According to the information in the graph, how much warmer is leaf temperature at the compensation point when light intensity is 11.5 kJ/m$^2$/min than when light intensity is 2.7 kJ/m$^2$/min? Express your answer in $^\circ$C to the nearest tenth.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is Leaf Temperature (°C), and the vertical axis is Carbon Dioxide Uptake (mg/g/hr). The solid lines represent photosynthetic rates under different light intensities; in the legend, 11.5 kJ/m²/min corresponds to the solid line with open squares, and 2.7 kJ/m²/min corresponds to the solid line with triangles; the dashed line represents respiration (respiration). Reasoning: The compensation point is the position where the photosynthetic rate and the respiration rate are equal, that is, the intersection of the corresponding solid line and the dashed line. Reading the graph shows that when the solid line for 11.5 kJ/m²/min intersects the dashed line, the leaf temperature is about 40.0°C; when the solid line for 2.7 kJ/m²/min intersects the dashed line, the leaf temperature is about 27.5°C. The temperature difference between the two is 40.0 − 27.5 = 12.5°C. Expressed to the nearest tenth, it is 12.5°C.

The dashed line plots the rate of respiration that occurs at the same time as photosynthesis. The compensation point occurs when photosynthesis and respiration rates are equal. According to the information in the graph, how much warmer is leaf temperature at the compensation point when light intensity is 11.5 kJ/m$^2$/min than when light intensity is 2.7 kJ/m$^2$/min? method.method_draft: First describe the graph: it has leaf temperature on the x-axis, carbon dioxide uptake on the y-axis, solid curves for photosynthesis at different light intensities, and a dashed respiration curve. From the text, compensation occurs where a photosynthesis curve equals the respiration curve. On the image, find the dashed curve's intersection with the 11.5 kJ/m²/min solid curve, reading about 40.0°C. Then find the dashed curve's intersection with the 2.7 kJ/m²/min solid curve, reading about 27.5°C. Subtract: 40.0 − 27.5 = 12.5°C, then report to the nearest tenth.

推理：补偿点是光合作用速率与呼吸作用速率相等的位置，也就是相应实线与虚线的交点。读图可见，11.5 kJ/m²/min 的实线与虚线相交时叶温约为 40.0°C；2.7 kJ/m²/min 的实线与虚线相交时叶温约为 27.5°C。二者温差为 40.0 − 27.5 = 12.5°C。按最近的十分之一表示为 12.5°C。
